name: MiniCLEAN
summary: MiniCLEAN was a low-background single-phase noble-liquid demonstrator at SNOLAB, developing liquid-argon/liquid-neon methods for WIMP searches.
detection_principle: Nearly 4π photodetector coverage records liquid scintillation. Clean materials, spatial selections and scintillation timing reduce backgrounds.

sites.name: SNOLAB
sites.location: Underground laboratory in the Creighton mine, Sudbury, Ontario
sites.site_status: Experiment site; see the phase descriptions

status.label: Completed
status.evidence: SNOLAB explicitly lists it as Completed: operation began in 2013 and decommissioning began in 2019.

science_scope: This record covers experiments that directly measure possible interactions between dark matter and ordinary matter. Published exclusion limits, background events and projected sensitivities do not constitute a dark-matter discovery.
